title: Worked Example 4
summary: A ladder against a wall makes a right-angled triangle — the ladder is the hypotenuse.
alt: Worked Example 4: A ladder leans against a vertical wall. Its top is 2.4 m above the ground and its foot is 0.5 m from the wall. Calculate the length of the ladder.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: A ladder leans against a **vertical wall**. The top of the ladder is **2.4 m** above the ground (**AC**) and the foot is **0.5 m** from the wall (**CB**). The wall meets the ground at a right angle, **∠C = 90°**. Find the length **x** of the ladder (**AB**).

steps.title: Spot the right angle
steps.narration: In ΔABC, **∠C = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **the ladder**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. The ladder is the hypotenuse — the side opposite the right angle.

steps.title: Pythagoras' theorem
steps.narration: **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{x^2} &= \role{legA}{CB^2} + \role{legB}{AC^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute the lengths
steps.narration: Replace each side by its length.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{x^2} &= \role{legA}{CB^2} + \role{legB}{AC^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{0.5^2} + \role{legB}{2.4^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square and add
steps.narration: Square each number, then add them.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{x^2} &= \role{legA}{CB^2} + \role{legB}{AC^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{0.5^2} + \role{legB}{2.4^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{0.25} + \role{legB}{5.76} \\ &= \role{hyp}{6.01}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 6.01 is not a perfect square, so use a calculator and round to 3 significant figures.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{x^2} &= \role{legA}{CB^2} + \role{legB}{AC^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{0.5^2} + \role{legB}{2.4^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{0.25} + \role{legB}{5.76} \\ &= \role{hyp}{6.01} \\ \role{hyp}{x} &= \sqrt{6.01} = \role{ans}{2.45\ \text{m}}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Turn it into 3D
steps.narration: Tap the **3D view** button on the drawing to see the ladder, wall and ground as a real 3D model, and drag to look around it.

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides **6 m** and **8 m**. Find the **hypotenuse**.

takeaways: Find the **right angle** first — the side opposite it is the **hypotenuse**.
To find the hypotenuse: **add** the squares of the two shorter sides, then take the **square root**.
The hypotenuse is always the **longest** side, so check that your answer is bigger than both of the other sides.

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.

notes.title: Rounding
notes.text: If the answer is not a whole number, give it to **3 significant figures** unless the question says otherwise.
